style: Boarded early in the morning while cargo discharge was still running
Asks a long series of detailed technical questions on the bridge
When a crew member cannot answer, he explains the answer himself
Checks records and plans in the Master and Chief Engineer cabins
Overall attitude was calm and fair

questions.q: What cargo discharge operations are going on?
Has the ECDIS been newly installed?
What checks and tests are carried out before a long sail?
Are all ECDIS tools, sensors and ENCs checked thoroughly?
Is the weekly latest update applied?
What is the chart compilation scale?
Has CATZOC been applied?
What are the BWL and ERWL and the security level?
Has the Chief Engineer crosschecked and signed the passage plan?
What are the safety settings and how are they applied?
Are there any defects in the bridge equipment?
What is the condition of both radars?
What is the difference between X band and S band radar?
What are the magnetron running hours?
What is the magnetron replacement policy from the radar manual?
How do you check PI and what are its uses and how do you apply it?
Which radar will you use in rain?
Which speed input will you use for collision avoidance?
How do you check the performance monitor and what are its uses?
What is the company policy for use of AIS for collision avoidance?
What is the UKC policy while at berth?
Why is the UKC at berth 1.5 percent of the ship's breadth?
What are the squat effects in shallow water and safety contours?
When and where will you not test the GMDSS annual battery load test?
Do you have the GMDSS shore based maintenance certificate?
How are you maintaining ENCs and charts for updating weekly?
What is AIO?
What is the ESD?
What is a static accumulator and is the cargo static or not?
Various deck questions
Various engine room questions
Various engine room questions
Various questions on fuel and MARPOL
Various document questions

checks.item: Full passage plan on ECDIS and paper plan
Navigation lights tested by removing fuse and lamp test
GMDSS log book, last monthly and weekly tests
Mooring, MSMP and line management checklists as per company policy

tips: Be ready for detailed ECDIS and radar questions including CATZOC, PI, magnetron hours and performance monitor
Know the UKC policy at berth and why it is 1.5 percent of breadth
Know GMDSS tests and when the annual battery load test is not done
Keep mooring, MSMP and line management checklists ready in the CCR
summary: Inspector boarded at 0520 LT at Manzanillo while cargo discharge was nearly complete. He did deck rounds, CCR, engine room, Chief Engineer and Master cabin checks, then a long detailed bridge session on ECDIS, radar, UKC and GMDSS. He was calm and fair, and when crew could not answer he explained the answer himself. Inspector name and port were given; date was not.
